answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on an attestation graph, limiting how far endorsements can carry influence. A sybil cluster resembling an island—whether labeled marble or dune—must connect to honest participants through external edges; if that cut is sparse, its conductance is low. Under suitable mixing and vote-weight assumptions, conductance and min-cut bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight rather than letting internal attestations amplify it without limit.
